Needs changes before merge. This is a safety-tier review. Set `needs-rework`.

Reviewed locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3503`. The trial merge with `upstream/main` is clean.
Base: `ef157211438104997fc9e51f7e3affc4db303545`.
Trial merge: `8dad8575638e5d70b5a7063820a1617166a7ff5b`.
Its first parent is the PR head above. No GitHub runner was used.
The law check used `git show upstream/main:AGENTS.md`.

**Requested before merge**

1. **[P1] Invalidate old Part caches, or check their kerf at the post.** `crates/app/src/operation/params/turning.rs:159` keeps the default stamp unchanged. The new check at `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:2963` runs only during generation. Thus a cache from the old centered kerf can still read fresh and post a gouge. I reproduced this with the 3 mm blade and the end face at Z-70. A temporary run used the actual `upstream/main` parting generator, without the new generation check, and saved its centered path. I then restored all PR code and opened that unmodified saved project. Its parameters, stamp, cached moves, and verdicts were not edited. The reopened operation was `Ok`. The full `posting::post_script` call passed and wrote `G01 X0. Z-71.5`. Its kerf reaches Z-68.5, 1.5 mm into the finished part. Add a Part-specific stamp salt or a live kerf check. Add a test that opens a cache from the old algorithm and refuses the post until regeneration. The supplied stack includes the change to the default algorithm, so it must also invalidate its old verdicts.
2. **[P2] Make the catalog suite green.** `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs:311` still requires `G01 X0. Z13.5`. The changed `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc:680` contains `G01 X0. Z12. F0.02`. The full `example_catalog` suite failed here: 36 passed, 1 failed, 4 ignored. Update the pin to the intended kerf and run the full suite again. The failure is in the supplied stack and still blocks this head.
3. **Add the UI evidence.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turning_page.rs:304` adds the kept-piece and back-stock controls. The PR body has no before/after screenshots. Link both views from the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Keep review images out of this PR branch.
4. **Correct “Goldens moved” in the PR body.** It says “None”, but the diff against current upstream main changes both `groove_part.nc` goldens and both catalog programs. List the millimetre and inch goldens, the cone-thread case, and the groove-part-off case. Include their project, script, and README changes. Identify the changes inherited from #3472. A stack still needs an accurate account of the programs in its diff.

**What passed**

The kept-side setting reaches generation, command validation, undo/redo, project storage, MCP, and the page draft. The new kernel tests detect the two repeated mutations below.

- The initial quick plan had 732 steps. I stopped that broad run after its post and motion suites passed. It is not a full quick pass. Its motion library result was 539 passed, 10 ignored. All 20 selected turning binaries passed, including `turning_part_kept` (5) and `turning_part_kerf` (6).
- The selected quick run had 11 steps: 10 passed and `app suites: example_catalog` failed. App library: 297 passed. UI library: 1,435 passed, 8 ignored. `catalog_groove_part_off`: 1; `coarse_laws`: 6; `drill_prior`: 12; `mcp_enum_patch`: 3; `mcp_part_kerf`: 1; `project_roundtrip`: 76; `setup_align_lathe`: 4; `turning`: 6. These passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

The catalog failure was:

```text
thread 'turning_cone_thread_case_posts_the_taper_and_the_thread' panicked at crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs:311:5:
the part-off reaches the axis
```

UI `catalog_render` also passed: 2 active tests, 1 ignored screenshot renderer. It ran from `crates/ui`. The full `example_catalog` suite also ran, with the failure above. The fixture-reader search covered the changed Fanuc lathe golden directories. This PR does not change an importer or add a STEP fixture, so the extra importer suites do not apply.

**Safety checks and mutations**

- Kernel forced to `chuck_side()` and the unshifted plane: RED, 3 of 5 `turning_part_kept` tests failed.
- Verdict used the plane instead of the back-stock flank: RED, `a_back_stock_moves_the_whole_kerf_into_the_bar` failed.
- Both mutations restored: GREEN, all 5 tests passed. The worktree has no source changes.
- Both legacy-cache probes reproduced finding 1. The second used an actual old-generator cache, without edits to the saved data. Its post gate had no problems. It said that the stock sim did not judge the turning program and that the generation verdict stood. The full post still succeeded. The probe sources were removed after the runs. All 8 `lathe_part_off_kerf` tests passed again after restoration.
- I checked every changed line in all four NC files. The millimetre golden moves its part-off from Z-11.5 to Z-13. The inch golden moves from Z-0.4528 to Z-0.5118. Both catalog programs move from Z13.5 to Z12 and drop one duplicate axis rung. No other NC section changed.

**Heavy lanes**

This review ran `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` locally on the trial merge above, with six jobs. The command reached its 40-minute limit and exited 124. The release build passed in 568 seconds. All 37 motion targets and 131 app targets passed. The command stopped during `app heavy: shared_face_bodies_finish`. No failed assertion was reported in this attempt. This is not a complete green heavy result.

**Not run - owed:** 75 app targets, listed below. The interrupted target is owed too. No `merge-ready` label is appropriate for this head.

**Notes**

The inherited cache-wrapper setting stalled before compilation. The wrapper also timed out on `rustc --version`. I stopped that attempt and ran the checks with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`. The local source and review evidence were not committed or pushed. The review worktree and branch remain for the next round. No real control or machine was exercised.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
